hostDefaults.bio: Travel Director on Xmas Whirl. Clear briefings, calm days and the practical details handled properly.
hostDefaults.profileTitle: Europe changed my life. Now I get to share that properly.
hostDefaults.profileIntro: I was born in the small rural town of Cobram, Australia. At 21, I set off on what was meant to be a six-week holiday to Europe and I never looked back. I fell completely in love with the continent, and its rich culture, deep history and vibrant way of life have shaped who I am ever since.
hostDefaults.profileStory: After 30 years on the road, many of them across TTC touring brands, I still feel it every time. The groups I love most span generations: young families and grandparents, honeymooners and seasoned travellers, all sharing the same coach, the same table and the same moments that make a trip memorable.
hostDefaults.profileWelcome: Whenever I can, I choose to be here, because I truly love Europe and everything it offers. I can't wait to share that love with you through stories, sights and unforgettable moments that bring this incredible continent to life.
hostDefaults.profileHighlightsTitle: The trips I enjoy most are the ones that feel warm, local and genuinely personal from the first day.

profileHighlights.title: Real local connections
profileHighlights.copy: The places I love most on tour are the family kitchens, workshops and side streets guests would never find alone.

profileHighlights.title: Groups that feel personal
profileHighlights.copy: My favourite tours are the ones where strangers become a table full of stories by the second night.

profileHighlights.title: A practical style on the road
profileHighlights.copy: I like guests to feel looked after, well briefed and relaxed enough to enjoy the day instead of worrying about logistics.

hostDefaults.secondaryHostBio: Our driver Gianfranco is a fantastic part of the team and has been driving coaches around Europe for the last 15 years plus. You'll find him to be a very safe and friendly driver.
hostDefaults.contactPreference: WhatsApp for quick questions, call for anything urgent, or email if you need something in writing.

emergency.label: Brendon Bush
emergency.note: Emergency calls preferred. Otherwise send a text/SMS or contact through hotel reception.

faq.question: When will I usually get the next day's details?
faq.answer: Use the app as the day-by-day source of truth. Admin notes can also be added for each day when you want to highlight a special meeting point, reminder or change.

faq.question: Where do I find experiences?
faq.answer: Open Itinerary, then switch to Experiences. Each experience is attached to the correct tour day, and uploaded admin images will appear there as well.

faq.question: What should I keep with me on coach days?
faq.answer: Keep your passport, wallet, phone, charger, any medication, weather layer and the items you will want before your checked luggage is unloaded at the hotel.

faq.question: How do I contact Brendon Bush quickly during the tour?
faq.answer: For emergencies, call Brendon directly. Otherwise send a text or SMS, or ask the hotel reception to help you make contact if the phone is off.

tipping.title: Restaurant
tipping.body: If coperto or a cover charge appears on your bill, no additional tip is needed. For a genuinely good meal, leave €2-€5 or 5-10%.

tipping.title: Pizza / casual dining
tipping.body: Leave the small change or round to the nearest euro.

tipping.title: Bar / coffee
tipping.body: Drop a coin on the counter. Small change is often appreciated for friendly service.

tipping.title: Local Specialist (guide)
tipping.body: Pass it directly at the end of the visit if you felt the difference.

tipping.title: Taxi
tipping.body: Round to the nearest euro. It is not standard to tip beyond that.

tipping.title: Travel Director
tipping.body: Paid in cash, in person, on the final night of the tour.

tipping.title: Coach Driver
tipping.body: Paid in cash, in person, on the final night of the tour.

practical.title: Keep in hand
practical.body: Passport, daily medication, phone, charger, wallet, light weather layer and anything needed before your luggage is delivered at the hotel.

practical.title: Coach days
practical.body: Please be ready a few minutes before departure times, keep essentials with you, and label your luggage clearly for smoother hotel arrivals.

practical.title: Money
practical.body: Cards are widely accepted, but a little local cash can still be useful for toilets, small purchases, markets and quick stops.

beforeYouGo.title: Travel documents
beforeYouGo.body: Please double-check passport validity, travel insurance, any required visas and any personal medical documents before departure.

beforeYouGo.title: Packing
beforeYouGo.body: Bring comfortable walking shoes, a light waterproof layer, charging cables, a reusable water bottle and clothes for both warm afternoons and cooler mornings.

beforeYouGo.title: Arrival day
beforeYouGo.body: Keep your arrival details handy and look out for your welcome meeting time inside the Day 1 schedule.
